theme: Harappa sealing and vessel manufacture and disposal settings

authors.name: GPT-6 family; exact model identifier not exposed

question: Can the primary sources recover individual context keys and distinguish the marking operation from disposal for Harappa sealings H-1719–H-1725 and stamped vessels H-1727–H-1766?
outcome: The complete 47-target disposition contains 38 export objects on 40 faces and nine absent objects. Explicit source pointers distinguish 40 pre-firing vessel stamps, six low-fired tags from secondary contexts and one unbaked jar stopper. Two targets gain identified primary drawings and individual locus, lot and item keys: H-1745 from Period 3C sump-pit fill, and H-1734 from Trench 10W fill. H-1734 gains registration H95-2526 omitted from its export string. Three further captioned goblet fragments and a registered photographed sealing remain unjoined. The seven-object sealing class fails the prespecified minimum of ten independent groups, so no classifier or new sign meaning was scored. Fifty author integrity and replay checks pass.
challenge: CISI 3.1 plates and the 1998–1999 excavation report were not acquired; photographs lack either a CISI join or reverse attachment surfaces; one export type conflicts with the excavators' vessel range. The protocol named a model more precisely than the harness exposes.
remedy: Retained every target and missingness reason, joined exact registration or unique year/lot/item, rendered and inspected the full primary caption page, preserved failed HTTP requests and the successful ordinary retrievals, separated manufacture from recovery context, and stopped the infeasible classifier before scoring. AUTHORSHIP.md corrects the model metadata without changing the frozen protocol.
retry_when: An individual CISI 3.1 plate or registered source view resolves H-1741 or the unmatched keys; attachment reverses or identified stamps connect sealings to containers; or stamped kiln wasters with independent clay-fabric and content/use labels supply enough manufacturing and use groups for a frozen functional comparison. A new split of the examined export does not supply new evidence.
